title: The case for travelling with less
text: Seasoned travellers {{1}} long known a paradox: {{2}} more you pack, the less you enjoy the journey. Everything must fit {{3}} one bag, and one bag means no queues at check-in, no waiting {{4}} luggage on a carousel, and no ruined plans {{5}} an airline sends your suitcase to the wrong country. Moving between cities becomes a five-minute errand {{6}} of a logistical operation. {{7}} is only when the weather turns unexpectedly that anyone notices the absence of a spare outfit, and even then most cities {{8}} you land will sell you another pair of socks within the hour.

gaps.explanation: Present perfect with a plural subject: have long known.

gaps.hint: article: ___ more you pack, the less
gaps.explanation: 'The more…, the less…' — the double comparative takes 'the'.

gaps.hint: time clause: no ruined plans ___ an airline
gaps.explanation: The ruin happens when the airline errs: when.

gaps.hint: adverb: an errand ___ of an operation
gaps.explanation: 'Instead of' — the replacement phrase; the gap is 'instead'.

gaps.hint: cleft pronoun: ___ is only when the weather turns
gaps.explanation: The cleft structure 'It is only when… that…'.
'Where' refers back to the cities as the place.
